read_scope.notes: Read the complete 22-page frozen PDF, including references and Appendices A–G, and visually inspected every rendered page. Inspected all five figures and all ten tables, with an additional enlarged inspection of page 9. Consulted frozen paper.tex and specificity_results.tex to resolve wording, notation and source locations. Technical appendices were treated as optional depth when judging main-text accessibility. Abstract contains 152 whitespace-delimited words after simple TeX normalization. No other reviews, versions, progress records, goals or non-snapshot manuscript were inspected.

score_reasons.expression: Excellent, precise and fluent prose. Sections 4.1–4.2 explain contrasts, aligned response and error with short sentences, an actual lightness comparison, and the 1/0/1 benchmark example before formal notation. The results distinguish point estimates, adjusted comparisons and descriptive diagnostics with consistent qualification. The remaining refinements concern the somewhat generic final synthesis of calibration and the isolated Figure 1 label “Original painting,” which is less precise than the surrounding reproduction terminology.
score_reasons.structure: The question, reference panel, controlled arms, measurement representation, score intuition, inference and results form a coherent progression. The primary finding leads Section 5.1, and Sections 5.3–5.5 visibly identify retrospective explanations and source sensitivity. Tables 2–4 efficiently connect the main comparison, decomposition/calibration and changed source-corrected intervals. Appendices preserve substantial technical evidence without making it necessary to reconstruct the main study. The brief discussion could synthesize the two calibration questions more explicitly, but no substantial reorganization is needed.
score_reasons.new_reader_understanding: The abstract is standalone and bounded, the six prompt clauses and repeat count are concrete, and Table 1 translates all feature families into recognizable visual properties. Section 4.1 supplies unusually useful numerical and idealized examples; Section 4.2 explicitly separates the theoretical D=1 benchmark from the generic-painting arm. Figure 2 provides common-scale detail views, while Figure 3 labels the reference-strength and no-distinction anchors. The only notable local gap is that the main-text calibration recipe does not explicitly say that the scalar is fitted separately for each model by minimizing training-scene error; the appendix resolves this.
score_reasons.engagement: The opening Monet/Sisley example makes the evaluation problem consequential. Figure 1 rewards inspection of the two controls and named conditions, and the text directs attention to a visible Cézanne contrast without treating it as perceptual validation. The positive-alignment/high-error result, uneven artist pairs and two distinct ordering changes sustain a discernible narrative. The compact discussion is accurate but could give the reader a sharper explanation of what the calibrated versus uncalibrated comparison reveals, rather than only saying that they answer different questions.

strengths: The Introduction explains why moving closer to Monet does not establish recovery of the Monet–Sisley distinction, making the central evaluation question understandable before notation.
Section 4.1 connects the actual .325 versus .254 lightness gaps to centering, then uses no distinction, exact recovery and doubled contrasts to explain why expected errors can be 1, 0 and 1.
Table 1 supplies plain-language interpretations of the 31 coordinates, and Section 3.3 clearly defines the development-IQR unit and equal coordinate weighting.

Figure 1 shows all six conditions for all six generators with an explicit selection rule; Figure 2 uses labeled, common-scale detail views to make the nearby Monet, Sisley and Pissarro contrasts inspectable.

Section 5.1 distinguishes detecting an aligned response from establishing performance below the no-distinction benchmark, and Table 4 openly displays the changed Sunburst and GPT Image 1 comparisons after source correction.

Calibration, painter-pair permutations, source audits and older cohorts are clearly marked as descriptive or retrospective; the manuscript repeatedly preserves the boundary between digital-reference agreement and perceptual artistic fidelity where that distinction affects interpretation.

findings.location: Section 4.4, p. 6, paper.tex lines 307–315; Section 6 opening, p. 10, paper.tex lines 321–324
findings.issue: The calibration recipe says that “we fit one nonnegative multiplier,” without explicitly identifying a separate fit for each model or the training-error objective. The discussion then says only that original and calibrated contrasts “answer different questions,” leaving those questions implicit. Appendix B.1 and the numerical examples make the intended procedure recoverable, so this is a localized main-text refinement.
findings.reader_effect: A reader can follow the numerical reversal but must infer the precise allowance made to each model and articulate for themselves what that reversal reveals about response magnitude versus residual pattern mismatch.
findings.suggested_change: Replace the fitting sentence with: “For each model, we choose a nonnegative multiplier that minimizes measured error on 13 scenes and evaluate it on the omitted scene, rotating through all 14 scenes.” Replace the generic discussion sentence with an equally compact synthesis: “Uncalibrated error evaluates the delivered painter contrasts; calibrated error asks how much disagreement remains after correcting their overall magnitude.” These substitutions use the existing evidence and need not increase the page count.

findings.issue: The row label “Original painting” is less precise than the caption and main text, which consistently identify the measured objects as historical digital reproductions, including audited crops.
findings.reader_effect: A reader scanning the image panel first briefly encounters a stronger object-level label than the carefully bounded reference target used throughout the study. The caption already supplies the correct interpretation.
findings.suggested_change: Replace the row label with “Reference reproduction” on two lines. Keep the existing caption, image selection and provenance unchanged.

summary: Excellent, largely self-contained scientific communication under the fixed rubric. The main narrative is readily understood, the visual evidence is legible, and the distinction between measured digital-reference agreement and artistic fidelity is maintained. Only localized clarification of the calibration question and a reference-image label is warranted; no new experiments, expanded scope or longer manuscript is needed.
